description: 0.9.3 keeps the full baked catalogue dormant in the JAR and builds a small active pack from each saved world. It enables the pack in save config, keeps fallback UVs native, and selects the clicked material from placement interaction data.
changes: Scan saved chunk palettes and write ZAS_ActivePack.zip before world startup
Move 0.9.1 fallback states onto native atlas and model geometry
Use matching interaction destination plus clicked target or block face to select the material
Retain material while local topology changes shape
Use current-view raycast only when no client interaction context exists
advantages: World loads with 56 active appearances in observed save
No texture rebuild or asset registration on placement
Existing saved block IDs remain valid
Unknown materials can be prepared for a future restart
disadvantages: A material first encountered during play may use stone until a later restart
Budget of 10 million HD pixels per world is a project guard, not a proven engine limit
Final click behavior lacks automated client trace
Full dedicated-server test was limited by native QUIC and shutdown errors
test_results: 0.9.1 pack load: 921 aliases, 56 appearances, zero runtime registrations
0.9.3 Gradle offline build passed with 12,124 assertions
Asset validation passed 34,300 geometry samples, 498 face mappings per atlas, 12,114 states and one creative item

metrics.reliability: User feedback positive; final click path not instrumented in client
metrics.performance: 4,784,128 active HD pixels for observed save; 56 appearances and 73 PNGs
